diagnosis: Customer on legacy_auth asks about Unified Auth migration process and reversibility. KB-0012 covers the migration steps and states it cannot be reversed once legacy tokens are disabled. No escalation required per policy.
reply: Thanks for reaching out about migrating to Unified Auth. Migration replaces your account-wide token with scoped keys. The recommended approach is a dual-running window: first create the scoped keys, then cut your traffic over to them, and only disable the legacy token once you're confident everything is working. One important note: migration cannot be reversed once legacy tokens are disabled, so we recommend validating your integrations thoroughly during the dual-running period before disabling the legacy token. Please let us know if you have any other questions as you plan the move.
